note: Generated by experiments/method_table/build_method_table.py; do not edit by hand. auc values are ROC-AUC on the synthetic anomaly corpus v2: withheld_band = rating bands 1300 and 1700, never seen in training (all substitution rates); rateNN = those bands at NN percent engine moves vs clean games; seen = the test partition of the training bands.
critical_moves_note: Critical moves and chart markers always rank by attention times deviation, whatever method is selected: every trained detector's per-move output localized engine moves at or below chance.

methods.label: Computed score (first method tried)
methods.description: The first method tried: the attention-weighted average gap, in rating points, between the rating model's per-move estimate and the player's baseline. It has no trained parameters.
methods.caveat: It separated engine-substituted games at about chance, so it is shown for comparison only.

methods.label: Trained detector (LightGBM)
methods.description: A gradient-boosted tree model scoring 0 to 1 from 97 whole-game summaries of the rating model's per-move estimates and attention plus simple board and clock facts.

methods.label: Per-move detector (A3g, default)
methods.description: A small recurrent network scoring 0 to 1 from the rating model's per-move estimates and attention plus simple board and clock facts, read move by move. It measured best of the four on rating bands withheld from training.

methods.label: Full model (CNN-BiLSTM)
methods.description: A fine-tuned copy of the rating model itself scoring 0 to 1 straight from the board positions and clocks, move by move.
methods.caveat: It trained on a split that was not twin-safe, so its withheld-band result is the fair comparison; a board-level model can also learn to spot engine-style moves directly.
